instruction: Choose a suitable finite-element simulation tool available in the current Windows fused environment. Use a command-line or scripting workflow. Use the selected finite-element simulation tool to build and solve a 2D axisymmetric finite-element model of a circular plate. Adopt the N-mm-MPa unit system throughout. Geometry: Create a 2D axisymmetric deformable solid part representing the circular plate cross-section. The radial extent is from r = 0 mm to r = 50 mm. The axial/thickness extent is from z = 0 mm to z = 1 mm. Material: Define a material named Steel. Set Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa and Poisson's ratio ν = 0.3. Assign this material to the entire plate section using a homogeneous solid section. Mesh and Element Type: Employ appropriate axisymmetric solid elements. Use a structured mesh with a radial seed size of 2.0 mm and one element through the thickness. Create the following node sets: AXIS on the r = 0 boundary, OUTER on the r = 50 mm boundary, and TOP on the z = 1 mm boundary. Boundary Conditions: On AXIS, constrain radial displacement U1 = 0. On OUTER, constrain both U1 = 0 and U2 = 0. Loading: Apply a downward pressure of 0.1 N/mm² on the TOP boundary, represented as equivalent axisymmetric concentrated nodal forces. For each top node at radius r_i, compute the force in the U2 direction as: F_i = -p × 2πr_i × Δr_i For the first and last top nodes, use half the adjacent radial interval for Δr_i. For interior top nodes, use half the distance between neighboring top nodes. The node at r = 0 carries zero equivalent force. Analysis: Create a static analysis step named Step-Pressure. Request field output for U, RF, and S. Create and submit a job named Job-Plate, and wait for successful completion. Deliverables: save the native model artifact and native solver result artifact on the Desktop, and write `C:/Users/user/Desktop/metrics.json` with numeric fields for the requested metrics.
